_comment: Hand triage of every finding in corpus-results.json. A corpus count with no triage behind it is the same defect as a benchmark score with no detector behind it. Any FALSE_POSITIVE entry fails CI: the rule must be fixed and a regression fixture added, not the entry edited.

false_positives_found_and_fixed_this_run.class: browser-automation import treated as an agent framework
false_positives_found_and_fixed_this_run.fix: playwright and selenium removed from reachability.agent_frameworks — driving a browser is not agent-reachability.

false_positives_found_and_fixed_this_run.class: module-level script setup treated as agent-reachable
false_positives_found_and_fixed_this_run.fix: module-level sinks no longer yield MEDIUM confidence (reachability.module_level_reachability, default false). Module scope runs at import time and cannot be selected by an LLM — the same reasoning that already excluded __main__ blocks. Measured precision of the signal on this corpus was 0/19.
false_positives_found_and_fixed_this_run.regression_fixture: covered by p12 (module-level) and the corpus itself

false_positives_found_and_fixed_this_run.class: inter-agent transport treated as external communication
false_positives_found_and_fixed_this_run.fix: COMMUNICATION-SEND rules gained exclude_receiver_types for A2A/event-bus/runtime receivers, mirroring the existing _is_db_receiver constraint. Matches the recorded r05 negative result.

RunStdioServer is a server bootstrap function, not a tool handler. cfg.LogFilePath is server configuration (set at startup), not model-controlled input. The Go detector's import-based reachability heuristic flags every function in a file that imports the agent framework, including infrastructure functions. The agent cannot influence which log file path is opened. Note: this finding was never in the original corpus-results.json because the corpus was assembled before Go support shipped (v1.1.2). It appears in fresh scans with Go support installed but is not counted in the corpus figure.

downloadLogContent is a helper function, not a tool handler. logURL is a URL returned by client.Actions.GetWorkflowJobLogs (the GitHub API), not directly model-controlled. The agent controls jobID/owner/repo, but the URL is always a GitHub-hosted log file URL — the agent cannot redirect http.Get to an arbitrary server. This is not SSRF; it is a GitHub API client fetching GitHub-hosted content. The Go detector's import-based reachability heuristic flags the function because the file imports the agent framework. Note: this finding was never in the original corpus-results.json because the corpus was assembled before Go support shipped (v1.1.2).

corrections.description: 2 agno findings (cookbook/.../external_tool_execution.py:29 and :38) were originally triaged as TRUE_POSITIVE. They are actually guarded by @tool(external_execution=True), agno's human-in-the-loop primitive. The scanner now recognises this flag as a framework-level guard (Work Order 4, Part 2.1). The findings no longer fire. The published precision figure in CORPUS_STUDY.md was corrected from 30/30 (100%) to 28/28 (100%) — the 2 false positives were found and fixed by the project itself before any maintainer was contacted.

7 findings (4 crewai, 3 semantic-kernel) were originally triaged as TRUE_POSITIVE. They are actually guarded by validation methods (_validate_query, validate_url, validate_file_path, _validate_url) that dominate the sink and are bound to the model-controlled parameter. The scanner now recognises validation-method names as guards (prefix match on validate_*, check_*, sanitize_*, verify_*, assert_*). The findings no longer fire. Combined with the earlier agno correction (2 findings), the total correction is 30 → 21 TRUE_POSITIVE.

Work Order 1.6 corpus re-measurement. The TS guard rewrite (WO1.5) was exercised on 1 TS sink candidate across the entire corpus (2,168 TS files, 140 sink candidates, 1 reached guard analysis). Zero TP findings changed. The github-mcp-server Go findings (2) were triaged for the first time — they were never in the original corpus-results.json because the corpus was assembled before Go support shipped (v1.1.2). Both are FALSE_POSITIVE: server.go:286 opens a server-config log file (not model-controlled); actions.go:172 fetches a GitHub API URL (not directly model-controlled). These 2 FALSE_POSITIVE findings are counted in the denominator: precision changed from 21/21 (100%) to 21/23 (91%). The true_positive count is unchanged at 21. Real-world TS validation (modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk, langchain-ai/langchainjs, getzep/zep-js) found 3 appeared findings in the MCP TypeScript SDK, all FALSE_POSITIVE: handler.fetch() is an MCP HTTP handler entry point (processes incoming requests), not outbound HTTP egress. The NET-EGRESS rule matches bare 'fetch', which matches handler.fetch(). These were previously suppressed by the lexical guard bug. The guard rewrite correctly removed the false-negative suppression, exposing the pre-existing rule-matching false positive. Fixed in Work Order 1.7.

corpus_exercised_ts_guard_rewrite.note: The corpus has 1 TS sink candidate that reached guard analysis. The TS guard rewrite (640 lines) was exercised on exactly 1 data point. Real-world validation was done separately on modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk (3 appeared, all FALSE_POSITIVE at the rule-matching level), langchain-ai/langchainjs (0 delta), and getzep/zep-js (0 delta).

measurement_note: Re-verified against 1.3.0 candidate (WO1.5+1.6+1.7+1.8). Zero findings changed from the 1.2.0 measurement. The TS guard rewrite (WO1.5) was exercised on 1 TS sink candidate in the corpus; the bare-pattern fixes (WO1.7+1.8) did not affect any corpus finding. The corpus figure remains 21 TP / 2 FP = 91%.
